content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Remaining useful life models can be updated sequentially using Bayesian methods when operating conditions drift, reducing prediction error on equipment monitored over months or years.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03304","field":"abstract","quote":"remaining useful life (RUL) models for rotating equipment are typically trained once and then applied statically, but operating conditions and load profiles drift over months or years"}]},{"text":"Hierarchical Bayesian models can estimate heterogeneous failure rates across machine populations from irregular inspection intervals and rank units by expected residual life to reduce unplanned outages.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03297","field":"abstract","quote":"hierarchical Bayesian Poisson–Gamma model for failure counts observed over irregular inspection intervals, allowing partial pooling of information"}]},{"text":"Multivariate time-series features extracted from sensor data can be systematically evaluated and reduced in dimensionality while retaining predictive power for downstream failure classification.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03296","field":"abstract","quote":"systematic comparison of 22 feature extraction approaches is presented for multivariate time-series data from rotating machinery"}]}],"fit":"strong","fitReason":"The researcher's publications directly address predictive maintenance ranking using Bayesian methods on heterogeneous equipment populations [SYN-PUB-03297], sequential model updating under changing conditions [SYN-PUB-03304], and feature extraction from time-series sensor data [SYN-PUB-03296], which are the core technical requirements for converting dissolved gas analysis and load data into transformer failure scores."}
